html:
A protest by students in Beijing on 4 May 1919 that grew into a nationwide movement and a turning point in modern Chinese thought. It pushed science, democracy and writing in everyday language, and it helped give birth to Chinese communism.

China had joined the Allies in the First World War. But at the Paris peace conference the victors gave the German rights in Shandong province to Japan instead of returning them to China. When news arrived, about three thousand students marched at Tiananmen. Strikes and boycotts spread to Shanghai and other cities, and China's delegates refused to sign the Treaty of Versailles.

The protest gave its name to a wider New Culture Movement. Writers and teachers attacked Confucian tradition as the root of China's weakness and called for "Mr Science and Mr Democracy". Lu Xun wrote fiction in the vernacular. Some leaders turned to Marxism after the Russian Revolution, and in 1921 they founded the Chinese Communist Party. The young Mao Zedong was among those swept up.
sum: A protest by students in Beijing on 4 May 1919 that grew into a nationwide movement and a turning point in modern Chinese thought. It pushed science, democracy and writing in everyday language, and it helped give birth to Chinese communism.
